text:
Elaine: Pushed a small Figma prototype for the compact rule-ordering gesture in routing editor. TL;DR: left-swipe on a rule row reveals a compact drag affordance + inline priority chip. thoughts?

Mike: I like the smaller footprint. Concern: discoverability for new users. can we add a short first-run hint or a subtle animated affordance? maybe a 2s tooltip on initial load.

Sophia: Contrast nit — the inline priority chip is too light at 14px; fails WCAG AA. Suggest using a stronger tint (e.g., #2563eb bg + white text) and bumping weight. Also keyboard focus state is currently invisible.

Jun: +1 on keyboard. Prototype currently requires a mouse drag. Need a keyboard reorder affordance (move up/down via a menu or modifiers) otherwise screenreader users can't reorder.

Aria L.: For SR behavior: give the row role='option' inside a listbox, and update aria-grabbed during drag. After move, announce: "Moved rule to position 3 of 8." That helps AT users confirm changes.

Design-bot: Quick screenshot/preview: https://figma.redwood/compact-ordering-proto — microcopy question: current hint says `Press and hold to drag` — feels modal. Maybe `Press M to move` is too prescriptive.

Elaine: Good call. Another UX detail: what happens when two rules end up with identical priority? Current validation text is terse: `Conflict — duplicate priority`. Feels abrupt and blocks flow.

Jun: Proposed copy: `Rule priorities must be unique. Use quick reorder or adjust priority to resolve.` — softer, actionable.

Mike: Also: if validation prevents saving, prefer non-blocking guidance — show inline warning + toast linking to the conflicting rules preview (so users can jump to the conflict) rather than modal.

Sophia: A11y nit for the preview toggle: don't rely on color alone to indicate "active" — add a visible label and focus ring. Disabled drag handle needs 3:1 contrast difference from background.

Aria L.: Simulation voice/announcements: when previewing/running simulated traffic, announce progress to assistive tech: e.g., `Simulating 3 of 12 requests — 25% complete`. Also announce final summary: `Simulation complete: 94% routed as expected.`

Elaine: Action items I'll own: 1) first-run hint + ephemeral tooltip (Mike) 2) keyboard reorder + ARIA roles/announcements (Jun + Aria L.) 3) color/contrast updates + focus styles (Sophia) 4) validation copy + non-blocking UX + preview link (Jun + Mike) 5) simulation progress announcements (Aria L.). I'll open tickets and link them here.

Mike: sgtm. target for prototype update: next Tue EOD? i'm OOO Fri.

Elaine: target Tue EOD. assigning myself + Sophia + Jun. ping me if blocked. :thumbsup: 

Jun: I'll draft keyboard interactions and paste a tiny example for review:
```
// keyboard reorder example (concept)
keydown: if (e.key === 'M' && row.focused) openMoveMenu();
moveUp(): swapPriorityWithAbove(); announce('Moved to position '+newIndex);
```

Sophia: I'll push contrast tweaks and update the priority chip variants in the figma file. will also add visible focus tokens.

Design-bot: Noted. I created placeholder tickets: RDW-4312 (hint & onboarding), RDW-4313 (keyboard reorder), RDW-4314 (contrast + focus), RDW-4315 (validation copy + non-blocking). linking here once PRs exist.

Elaine: Thanks all — nice catch on the SR announcements. We'll review the updated prototype in next design sync. :)
